---
title: "Do LLMs Stereotype Communication Apprehension?"
subtitle: "Tiered persona prompts, PRCA ground truth, and prediction error across demographic context"
author:
  - name: Jack J. Burleson
    url: https://github.com/Exios66
    affiliations:
      - University of Wisconsin–Madison
    corresponding: true
date: last-modified
abstract: |
  Large language models (LLMs) are increasingly asked to stand in for human respondents
  in survey and measurement research. This manuscript asks whether an LLM prompted to
  personify Prolific participants recovers their self-reported communication apprehension
  (CA), and whether prediction error tracks demographic or contextual cues systematically
  (stereotyping). Using McCroskey’s PRCA group and interpersonal subscales (range 6–30),
  we join Prolific demographics to Qualtrics responses, build cumulative persona prompts
  (demographics → employment → geography → transportation), and score predictions against
  ground-truth PRCA. Primary research focuses (RQ1–RQ3) ask whether employment status,
  transportation-use cues, and joint geo/employment/transit context improve absolute CA
  prediction error and alter demographic bias patterns. All displayed statistics use the
  full Prolific↔Qualtrics matched analytic cohort (N = 241; 101 regular / 140 non-regular
  weekly+ transit riders).

  Beyond those persona-tier questions, the project runs a parallel set of secondary
  observational research questions on the same matched sample. These reverse the predictive
  direction of the persona work: instead of asking whether transit information improves CA
  prediction, they ask how CA, place, and mobility self-reports relate to regular
  public-transit use (Q26 weekly-or-more), estimated with classical Random Forests rather
  than LLM inference. The secondary track is organized as five questions: (S1) mean CA
  differences for regular vs non-regular riders; (S2) whether survey geolocation (lat/long)
  predicts regular transit; (S3) whether group and interpersonal CA scores predict regular
  transit; (S4) whether mobility items—especially transit-day intensity (Q27) and ride-share
  days (Q28)—carry traditional-ML signal for the same outcome; and (S5) wave-2 follow-ups
  comparing car access, employment, demographics, country vs coordinates, Q28 conditioned on
  car access, joint CA+mobility models, and residual CA after ride-share.

  On a deterministic mock LLM, group-CA mean absolute error (MAE) ranges from 7.84
  (`demos`) to 8.56 (`geo`) across research tiers (transit = 8.01)—well above the
  classical suite floor (best transit group MAE = 4.49 Ridge). On the same cohort,
  traditional Random Forests show that ride-share days (Q28) predict regular transit at
  CV ROC-AUC = 0.762, whereas transit-day intensity (Q27) yields AUC = 0.589; geography
  (0.551) and CA scores (0.590) remain near chance. Extended follow-ups show Q28 retains
  lift after car access, demographics (especially age) modestly predict ridership, and CA
  adds little once Q28 is known. A kitchen-sink mobility+demo forest reaches AUC = 0.824
  but remains Q28-dominated. Together, the primary and secondary results clarify which
  mobility cues belong in persona tiers and which reverse predictors of transit habits
  carry the strongest tabular signal in this sample.
keywords:
  - communication apprehension
  - large language models
  - persona prompting
  - PRCA-24
  - algorithmic bias
  - public transit
  - ride-share
  - random forests
  - Prolific
  - Qualtrics
  - PSYCH 755
nocite: |
  @breiman2001, @pedregosa2011, @prolific, @qualtrics, @positconnect, @github, @psych755repo
---

#| include: false

if sibling_data_available():

    DATA_SOURCE = cohort_source_label()

        prolific_path=PROLIFIC,

else:

        COMMITTED_FULL / "participants.csv",
        COMMITTED_FULL / "evaluation.csv",
        COMMITTED_FULL / "summary.csv",
        COMMITTED_FULL / "source.json",
        SECONDARY_PATH,
    ]
    missing = [p for p in required if not p.is_file()]
    if missing:

            "Full-cohort File A/B/C not staged and committed Posit artifacts "
            f"are missing: {missing}"
        )
    meta = json.loads((COMMITTED_FULL / "source.json").read_text(encoding="utf-8"))
    if meta.get("data_source") == "excerpts" or int(meta.get("n_analytic", 0)) < 100:
        raise RuntimeError(f"Refusing excerpt-scale Posit artifacts: {meta}")
    DATA_SOURCE = meta.get("data_source", "artifacts/posit_full_cohort")

    evaluation = pd.read_csv(COMMITTED_FULL / "evaluation.csv")

        "participants": COMMITTED_FULL / "participants.csv",
        "evaluation": COMMITTED_FULL / "evaluation.csv",

if len(participants) < 100:

prompts = build_persona_prompts(participants, tiers=list(TIERS))

# Research-tier MAE table (exclude aggregate "all" and free-text "full" for primary bars)
mae_tiers = (
    summary[summary["tier"].isin(RESEARCH_TIERS)]

    .set_index("tier")

N = int(len(participants))

# Precompute employment MAE at transit tier for prose claims
_emp_mae = (

    .mean()
)
EMP_MAE_FULL = float(_emp_mae.get("Full-Time", float("nan")))
EMP_MAE_PART = float(_emp_mae.get("Part-Time", float("nan")))
EMP_MAE_OTHER = float(_emp_mae.get("Other", float("nan")))

# Base-demos stereotyping slice: student status at demos tier
_stu_mae = (
    evaluation.loc[evaluation["tier"] == "demos"]
    .groupby("Student status", dropna=False)["abs_error_group"]
    .mean()
)
STU_MAE_YES = float(_stu_mae.get("Yes", float("nan")))
STU_MAE_NO = float(_stu_mae.get("No", float("nan")))

_mae_idx = mae_tiers.set_index("tier")
MAE_GROUP_DEMOS = float(_mae_idx.loc["demos", "mae_group"])
MAE_GROUP_TRANSIT = float(_mae_idx.loc["transit", "mae_group"])
MAE_IP_DEMOS = float(_mae_idx.loc["demos", "mae_interpersonal"])
MAE_IP_TRANSIT = float(_mae_idx.loc["transit", "mae_interpersonal"])
BAND_GROUP_DEMOS = float(_mae_idx.loc["demos", "band_acc_group"])
BAND_GROUP_TRANSIT = float(_mae_idx.loc["transit", "band_acc_group"])
MAE_GROUP_DELTA = MAE_GROUP_TRANSIT - MAE_GROUP_DEMOS

# Introduction

Communication apprehension (CA) is a well-studied individual difference describing fear or anxiety associated with real or anticipated communication [@mccroskey1970; @mccroskey1984]. The Personal Report of Communication Apprehension (PRCA-24) yields context-specific subscale scores—including **group discussion** and **interpersonal** conversation—each ranging from 6 (very low apprehension) to 30 (very high) [@mccroskey1982; @beatty1988].

Separately, LLMs can be prompted to adopt demographic “personas” and emit survey-like responses. Prior work shows that such prompts can surface social stereotypes and opinion distributions that do not faithfully track the populations they purport to represent [@cheng2023; @santurkar2023]. That raises a concrete measurement question for psychological research tooling:

> When predicting an individual’s CA from demographic attributes alone, does an LLM’s prediction error correlate systematically with demographic group membership—i.e., does the model stereotype certain groups as more or less anxious than they actually reported being?

## Research focus

The primary design compares **information tiers** rather than a single prompt: each participant is personified five ways (`demos` → `employment` → `geo` → `transit` → `full`) while ground-truth PRCA stays fixed. The research focuses below ask whether accumulated context shrinks prediction error and whether residual error still clusters by group membership [@cheng2023; @santurkar2023].

::: {.research-focus-block}
### Primary research focuses — LLM persona tiers

**Outcome.** Continuous PRCA-24 group and interpersonal CA (6–30).  
**Design.** Cumulative persona prompts; MAE, signed error, and band accuracy vs Qualtrics ground truth.

| ID | Research question | What success looks like |
|:--:|:---|:---|
| **RQ1** | Does **employment status** improve CA prediction over demographics alone, and does it change the bias pattern? | Lower MAE at `employment` vs `demos`; smaller or more even error gaps across employment groups |
| **RQ2** | Does **transportation-use** information improve CA prediction, and does the model use it sensibly? | Lower MAE at `transit` vs earlier tiers; sensible use of mobility cues (not stereotype-only) |
| **RQ3** | Does combining employment, geography, and transit help beyond either alone, or are the cues redundant? | Joint tiers beat the better single addition, or plateau if signal overlaps |
:::

::: {.research-focus-block}
### Secondary research questions — predictors of regular transit use

**Outcome.** Binary regular public-transit use from Qualtrics `Q26` (`4-8 days a month` or `8 or more days a month`).  
**Design.** Classical Random Forests with stratified 5-fold CV (`random_state=42`) on the same Prolific↔Qualtrics matched sample (**N = 241**) — not LLM inference [@breiman2001; @pedregosa2011; @prolific].

| ID | Research question | Primary finding (seed = 42) | Sources |
|:--:|:---|:---|:---|
| **S1** | Do regular riders differ in **group / interpersonal CA** from non-regular riders? | Yes — lower CA among regulars (group Δ = −2.72, *d* = −0.46; interpersonal Δ = −1.73, *d* = −0.30); not a high-CA rider stereotype | [memo](memos/transit_riders_ca.md) · [write-up](docs/secondary_rq_transit_ca.md) |
| **S2** | Does survey **latitude / longitude** predict regular transit? | Near chance (CV ROC-AUC = **0.551**; country-only = 0.549) | [memo](memos/geo_predicts_transit.md) · [write-up](docs/secondary_rq_geo_predicts_transit.md) |
| **S3** | Do **group & interpersonal CA** scores predict regular transit? | Modest (CV ROC-AUC = **0.590**; group-only = 0.555; interpersonal-only = 0.506) | [memo](memos/ca_scores_predict_transit.md) · [write-up](docs/secondary_rq_ca_predicts_transit.md) |
| **S4** | Do **Q27** (transit intensity) and **Q28** (ride-share days) predict regular transit? | **Q28** AUC = **0.762**; **Q27** AUC = **0.589** and redundant beside Q28 (joint = 0.761) | [memo](memos/q27_q28_predict_transit.md) · [write-up](docs/secondary_rq_q27_q28_predict_transit.md) · [follow-ups](memos/transit_covariate_followups.md) |
| **S5** | Wave-2 follow-ups: demographics, country vs coordinates, Q28 \| car access, joint CA+mobility, residual CA after ride-share | Q28 retains lift after car access (+0.066 AUC); age/demos modest (0.618); CA adds +0.021 once Q28 is known | [agenda](docs/research_memo_agenda.md) · [write-up](docs/secondary_rq_followup_experiments.md) |
:::

Supporting methods pages: [cohort EDA](docs/cohort_eda.md), [ML baselines](docs/ml_baselines.md), [ML vs LLM metrics](docs/ml_vs_llm.md), and [feature importance](docs/factor_feature_importance.md). # Methods

## Data sources

Participants were recruited via Prolific [@prolific] in two waves (File A + File B; stacked) and completed a Qualtrics [@qualtrics] instrument (File C). Private full-cohort exports are not committed to git. **All statistics on this site use the full matched analytic cohort**: 252 Prolific∩Qualtrics matches → **N = 241** with complete scorable PRCA. The join key is Prolific `Participant id` ↔ Qualtrics `Q0`. Cleaning retains inner-join respondents with complete PRCA group and interpersonal items so every information tier shares the same ground-truth targets.

```{python}
#| label: tbl-sample
#| tbl-cap: "Analytic Sample Composition for the Full Matched Cohort"
#| tbl-colwidths: [40, 60]

def _label_counts(series: pd.Series) -> pd.Series:
    """Value counts with missing coded as Missing (avoid displaying 'nan')."""
    labeled = series.fillna("Missing").astype(str).replace({"nan": "Missing", "<NA>": "Missing"})
    return labeled.value_counts(dropna=False)


sex_counts = _label_counts(participants["Sex"])
emp_counts = _label_counts(participants["Employment status"])
stu_counts = _label_counts(participants["Student status"])
cty_counts = _label_counts(participants["Country of residence"]).head(5)
pd.DataFrame(
    [
        {"Metric": "Analytic N (complete PRCA)", "Value": f"{N}"},
        {
            "Metric": "Group CA M (SD)",
            "Value": f"{participants['gt_group_ca'].mean():.2f} ({participants['gt_group_ca'].std():.2f})",
        },
        {
            "Metric": "Interpersonal CA M (SD)",
            "Value": f"{participants['gt_interpersonal_ca'].mean():.2f} ({participants['gt_interpersonal_ca'].std():.2f})",
        },
        {
            "Metric": "Sex",
            "Value": "; ".join(f"{k} = {v}" for k, v in sex_counts.items()),
        },
        {
            "Metric": "Student status (base demos)",
            "Value": "; ".join(f"{k} = {v}" for k, v in stu_counts.items()),
        },
        {
            "Metric": "Employment status",
            "Value": "; ".join(f"{k} = {v}" for k, v in emp_counts.items()),
        },
        {
            "Metric": "Top countries of residence",
            "Value": "; ".join(f"{k} = {v}" for k, v in cty_counts.items()),
        },
        {
            "Metric": "Regular transit prevalence (Q26 weekly+)",
            "Value": f"{secondary['n_regular']}/{N} = {secondary['prevalence']:.3f}",
        },
    ]
)
```

::: {.callout-note}
## Full cohort only
Every table and figure uses the File A/B/C matched analytic sample (**N = 241**). Posit Connect Cloud loads committed artifacts under `artifacts/posit_full_cohort/` when private exports are absent. Excerpt fixtures are reserved for unit tests and are never displayed here.
:::

## Ground-truth PRCA scoring

Group items (`Q1`–`Q6`) and interpersonal items (`Q13`–`Q18`) use five-point Likert labels mapped to 1–5. Comfort-oriented items are reverse-coded as $6 - x$. Each subscale is the sum of six items (range 6–30). Classroom bands follow low ≤ 13, moderate 14–19, and high ≥ 20.

```{python}
#| label: tbl-gt-summary
#| tbl-cap: "Descriptive Statistics for Ground-Truth PRCA Subscales (N = 241)"

gt = (
    participants[["gt_group_ca", "gt_interpersonal_ca"]]
    .rename(
        columns={
            "gt_group_ca": "Group CA",
            "gt_interpersonal_ca": "Interpersonal CA",
        }
    )
    .describe()
    .T[["count", "mean", "std", "min", "25%", "50%", "75%", "max"]]
    .round(2)
)
gt
```

## Persona tiers

Persona prompts are cumulative and follow the **AI Terrarium / ICA 2026** digital-twin framing: what the LLM receives as the *user* message is a fluent second-person narrative (“You are a …”) plus a short CA self-report ask — not a bullet-list profile, and not the system prompt. The system message (omitted below) only sets inhabitance and the JSON response contract [@quarto]. Full Prolific waves omit ethnicity / nationality / language; the `demos` tier therefore uses Age, Sex, Country of residence, and Student status. Additional curated samples live under [`prompts/examples/`](prompts/examples/).

| # | Tier | Context added relative to the previous tier |
|:--:|---|---|
| 1 | `demos` | Age, sex, country of residence, student status |
| 2 | `employment` | + employment status |
| 3 | `geo` | + approximate survey lat/long (1 decimal) |
| 4 | `transit` | + public transit / ride-share / license / car access |
| 5 | `full` | + Qualtrics free-response attitudes (Q18.1 / Q19) |

The five listings below are **user prompts only** for the **same** analytic participant, so each step visibly accumulates context.

```{python}
#| label: persona-tier-progression
#| echo: false
#| output: asis

from ca_personas.personas import TIERS, build_persona_prompt, voice_sentences

# Prefer a participant whose five user prompts strictly grow in length and
# whose `full` tier includes free-response voice — so viewers can see the
# progressive context stack (demos → employment → geo → transit → full).
tier_labels = {
    "demos": "1. demos — base demographics",
    "employment": "2. employment — demos + work status",
    "geo": "3. geo — employment + place coordinates",
    "transit": "4. transit — geo + mobility self-reports",
    "full": "5. full — transit + free-response attitudes",
}

example_row = None
example_prompts = None
for _, row in participants.iterrows():
    if not voice_sentences(row):
        continue
    built = {t: build_persona_prompt(row, t) for t in TIERS}
    lengths = [len(built[t].user_prompt) for t in TIERS]
    if all(lengths[i] < lengths[i + 1] for i in range(len(lengths) - 1)):
        if all(built[t].user_prompt.lstrip().startswith("You are") for t in TIERS):
            example_row = row
            example_prompts = built
            break

if example_row is None or example_prompts is None:
    example_row = participants.iloc[0]
    example_prompts = {t: build_persona_prompt(example_row, t) for t in TIERS}

pid_short = str(example_row["participant_id"])[:12] + "…"
print(
    f"*Same participant throughout (`{pid_short}`); user message only — "
    "second-person persona narrative + CA ask (system prompt omitted).*\n"
)

for tier in TIERS:
    user = example_prompts[tier].user_prompt.strip()
    if not user.startswith("You are"):
        raise AssertionError(f"Expected Terrarium narrative for tier={tier}")
    stale_markers = ("Demographics:", "Adopt the following", "Fully personify")
    if any(marker in user for marker in stale_markers):
        raise AssertionError(f"Stale checklist-style prompt leaked for tier={tier}")
    print(f"### {tier_labels[tier]}\n")
    print("```text")
    print(user)
    print("```\n")
```

## Model calling and classical baselines

The Python package `ca_personas` supports Ollama, OpenRouter, and a deterministic **mock** provider for credential-free Posit renders [@ollama; @openrouter]. Predicted JSON fields are validated to the legal 6–30 range, then joined to ground truth for signed and absolute errors.

A seven-model tabular suite (Ridge, Elastic Net, k-NN, Random Forest, HistGradientBoosting, XGBoost, MLP) on the same tiers and targets is reported in [`docs/ml_baselines.md`](docs/ml_baselines.md). On the full cohort, the **best** group-CA MAE reaches **4.49** at `transit` (Ridge; RF = 4.68); the best interpersonal MAE reaches **4.25** (Elastic Net; MLP = 4.31). Feature attributions and ML-vs-LLM comparisons are documented in [`docs/factor_feature_importance.md`](docs/factor_feature_importance.md), [`docs/ml_vs_llm.md`](docs/ml_vs_llm.md), and [`memos/feature_predictive_power_ml_llm.md`](memos/feature_predictive_power_ml_llm.md).

# Results

## Mock LLM prediction error by information tier

On the full analytic cohort (**N = 241**), the offline mock LLM yields the MAE values in @tbl-mae. Group-CA MAE moves from **`{python} f"{MAE_GROUP_DEMOS:.2f}"`** at `demos` to **`{python} f"{MAE_GROUP_TRANSIT:.2f}"`** at `transit` (Δ = `{python} f"{MAE_GROUP_DELTA:+.2f}"`). Interpersonal-CA MAE is **`{python} f"{MAE_IP_DEMOS:.2f}"`** at `demos` and **`{python} f"{MAE_IP_TRANSIT:.2f}"`** at `transit`. Band accuracy for group CA is **`{python} f"{BAND_GROUP_DEMOS:.3f}"`** (`demos`) vs **`{python} f"{BAND_GROUP_TRANSIT:.3f}"`** (`transit`). These mock figures establish the measurement pipeline; they are not claims about a production LLM. These mock figures do **not** meet the RQ1/RQ2 success criterion of lower MAE with richer tiers (group MAE rises from demos to geo before a partial recovery at transit). Live-provider comparisons should be read against the full ML suite ceiling in [`docs/ml_baselines.md`](docs/ml_baselines.md) (best group MAE = **4.49** Ridge; best interpersonal = **4.25** Elastic Net at `transit`; RF group = 4.68).

```{python}
#| label: tbl-mae
#| tbl-cap: "Mock LLM Mean Absolute Error and Band Accuracy by Persona Tier (N = 241)"

disp = mae_tiers[
    [
        "tier",
        "n_with_ground_truth",
        "mae_group",
        "mae_interpersonal",
        "band_acc_group",
        "band_acc_interpersonal",
    ]
].copy()
disp.columns = [
    "Tier",
    "n",
    "MAE group",
    "MAE interpersonal",
    "Band acc. group",
    "Band acc. interpersonal",
]
disp = disp.round({"MAE group": 2, "MAE interpersonal": 2, "Band acc. group": 3, "Band acc. interpersonal": 3})
disp
```

```{python}
#| label: fig-mae
#| fig-cap: "Mean Absolute Error for Group and Interpersonal Communication Apprehension by Persona Information Tier"
#| fig-alt: "Grouped grayscale bar chart of mock-LLM MAE for group and interpersonal CA across demos, employment, geo, and transit tiers on N=241."
#| out-width: "90%"

fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=(7.2, 4.2))
grouped_bars(
    ax,
    list(mae_tiers["tier"]),
    {
        "Group CA": mae_tiers["mae_group"].tolist(),
        "Interpersonal CA": mae_tiers["mae_interpersonal"].tolist(),
    },
    ylabel="Mean absolute error",
    xlabel="Persona information tier",
    ylim=(0, 11),
)
fig.tight_layout()
plt.show()
```

*Note.* Mock LLM provider; full matched analytic cohort (N = 241). Lower MAE indicates closer recovery of ground-truth PRCA scores (range 6–30). See [`memos/feature_predictive_power_ml_llm.md`](memos/feature_predictive_power_ml_llm.md) for SHAP/F1 attributions on the same cohort.

## Predicted versus observed group CA

@fig-error-scatter shows predicted versus ground-truth group CA for each research tier. Points cluster away from the identity line, consistent with MAE values near 7–8 points on a 24-point scale. Compare panels against the cohort MAE path from `{python} f"{MAE_GROUP_DEMOS:.2f}"` (`demos`) to `{python} f"{MAE_GROUP_TRANSIT:.2f}"` (`transit`).

```{python}
#| label: fig-error-scatter
#| fig-cap: "Predicted Versus Ground-Truth Group Communication Apprehension Scores by Persona Tier"
#| fig-alt: "Four-panel grayscale scatterplots of predicted versus observed group CA for demos, employment, geo, and transit tiers with identity lines."
#| out-width: "100%"

tiers_plot = list(RESEARCH_TIERS)
fig, axes = plt.subplots(2, 2, figsize=(7.8, 7.4), sharex=True, sharey=True)
axes = axes.ravel()
for ax, tier in zip(axes, tiers_plot):
    frame = evaluation[evaluation["tier"] == tier]
    scatter_identity(
        ax,
        frame["gt_group_ca"],
        frame["pred_group_ca"],
        xlabel="Ground-truth group CA",
        ylabel="Predicted group CA",
        lims=(6, 30),
    )
    ax.text(
        0.04,
        0.96,
        f"{tier}\nMAE = {mae_tiers.loc[mae_tiers['tier']==tier, 'mae_group'].iloc[0]:.2f}",
        transform=ax.transAxes,
        va="top",
        ha="left",
        fontsize=9,
        bbox=dict(boxstyle="round,pad=0.2", facecolor="white", edgecolor="none", alpha=0.85),
    )
    # keep only one legend
    leg = ax.get_legend()
    if leg is not None and tier != "demos":
        leg.remove()
fig.tight_layout()
plt.show()
```

*Note.* Each panel contains N = 241 participant predictions from the mock LLM. The dashed line is the identity (perfect prediction).

## Absolute group-CA error by student status (base demos)

@tbl-by-student reports mock-LLM absolute group-CA error by **student status** — a first-class field in the base `demos` layer — crossed with persona tier. At the `demos` tier, Student = Yes MAE = `{python} f"{STU_MAE_YES:.2f}"` and Student = No MAE = `{python} f"{STU_MAE_NO:.2f}"`. Residual gaps here are the demographics-only stereotyping diagnostic before employment or transit cues are added ([`docs/ml_vs_llm.md`](docs/ml_vs_llm.md); [`docs/cohort_eda.md`](docs/cohort_eda.md)).

```{python}
#| label: tbl-by-student
#| tbl-cap: "Mock LLM Absolute Group-CA Error by Student Status and Persona Tier (Base Demos Layer)"

by_stu = (
    evaluation.dropna(subset=["abs_error_group"])
    .groupby(["Student status", "tier"], dropna=False)["abs_error_group"]
    .agg(n="count", MAE="mean", SD="std")
    .reset_index()
)
by_stu = by_stu[by_stu["tier"].isin(RESEARCH_TIERS)].copy()
by_stu["tier"] = pd.Categorical(by_stu["tier"], categories=list(RESEARCH_TIERS), ordered=True)
by_stu = by_stu.sort_values(["Student status", "tier"])
by_stu = by_stu.round({"MAE": 2, "SD": 2})
by_stu.columns = ["Student status", "Tier", "n", "MAE", "SD"]
by_stu
```

## Absolute group-CA error by employment status

@tbl-by-employment reports mock-LLM absolute group-CA error by employment status and tier. At the `transit` tier, Full-Time respondents show MAE = `{python} f"{EMP_MAE_FULL:.2f}"`, Part-Time MAE = `{python} f"{EMP_MAE_PART:.2f}"`, and Other MAE = `{python} f"{EMP_MAE_OTHER:.2f}"`. Systematic MAE gaps by employment are the stereotyping-relevant contrast named in RQ1; interpret mock gaps as pipeline diagnostics until a live provider is substituted ([`docs/ml_vs_llm.md`](docs/ml_vs_llm.md)).

```{python}
#| label: tbl-by-employment
#| tbl-cap: "Mock LLM Absolute Group-CA Error by Employment Status and Persona Tier (N = 241)"

by_emp = (
    evaluation.dropna(subset=["abs_error_group"])
    .groupby(["Employment status", "tier"], dropna=False)["abs_error_group"]
    .agg(n="count", MAE="mean", SD="std")
    .reset_index()
)
by_emp = by_emp[by_emp["tier"].isin(RESEARCH_TIERS)].copy()
by_emp["tier"] = pd.Categorical(by_emp["tier"], categories=list(RESEARCH_TIERS), ordered=True)
by_emp = by_emp.sort_values(["Employment status", "tier"])
by_emp = by_emp.round({"MAE": 2, "SD": 2})
by_emp.columns = ["Employment status", "Tier", "n", "MAE", "SD"]
by_emp
```

## Secondary results: regular transit and mobility predictors

**Regular transit** is defined as `Q26` ∈ {`4-8 days a month`, `8 or more days a month`} (weekly-or-more), yielding **101 regular / 140 not regular** riders (prevalence = **0.419**) in the analytic cohort. The analyses below use stratified 5-fold Random Forests (`random_state=42`) unless noted. Full write-ups: [`memos/transit_riders_ca.md`](memos/transit_riders_ca.md), [`memos/geo_predicts_transit.md`](memos/geo_predicts_transit.md), [`memos/ca_scores_predict_transit.md`](memos/ca_scores_predict_transit.md), [`memos/q27_q28_predict_transit.md`](memos/q27_q28_predict_transit.md), [`memos/transit_covariate_followups.md`](memos/transit_covariate_followups.md).

### Regular riders differ in CA scores

Welch tests on the matched cohort show lower CA among regular riders ([memo](memos/transit_riders_ca.md)):

| Subscale | M regular (n=101) | M not regular (n=140) | Δ | Cohen's d | Welch p | 95% bootstrap CI for Δ |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---|
| Group CA | 13.04 | 15.76 | −2.72 | −0.46 | .0003 | [−4.15, −1.28] |
| Interpersonal CA | 13.31 | 15.04 | −1.73 | −0.30 | .020 | [−3.12, −0.25] |

```{python}
#| label: fig-transit-ca-means
#| fig-cap: "Mean Ground-Truth PRCA Scores for Regular Versus Non-Regular Public-Transit Riders"
#| fig-alt: "Grouped grayscale bar chart of mean group and interpersonal CA for regular and non-regular transit riders."
#| out-width: "75%"

g = secondary["transit_ca"]["group"]
i = secondary["transit_ca"]["interpersonal"]
fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=(6.4, 4.0))
grouped_bars(
    ax,
    ["Group CA", "Interpersonal CA"],
    {
        f"Regular (n={g['n_regular']})": [g["mean_regular"], i["mean_regular"]],
        f"Not regular (n={g['n_not_regular']})": [g["mean_not_regular"], i["mean_not_regular"]],
    },
    ylabel="Mean PRCA score (6–30)",
    ylim=(0, 22),
)
fig.tight_layout()
plt.show()
```

*Note.* Full matched analytic cohort. Means correspond to the Welch contrasts reported above and in [`memos/transit_riders_ca.md`](memos/transit_riders_ca.md).

### Geography and CA as classifiers of regular transit

On the same outcome, a lat/long Random Forest yields CV ROC-AUC = **0.551** (country-only AUC = **0.549**; chance = **0.500**) ([memo](memos/geo_predicts_transit.md)). A Random Forest on group + interpersonal CA yields CV ROC-AUC = **0.590** (group-only = **0.555**; interpersonal-only = **0.506**; OOF confusion TN=76, FP=64, FN=40, TP=61) ([memo](memos/ca_scores_predict_transit.md)).

```{python}
#| label: fig-geo-ca-auc
#| fig-cap: "Cross-Validated ROC-AUC for Geography and Communication-Apprehension Random Forests Predicting Regular Transit"
#| fig-alt: "Horizontal grayscale bar chart comparing ROC-AUC for lat/long, country-only, CA joint, CA ablations, and chance."
#| out-width: "85%"

labels = [
    "CA: group + interpersonal",
    "CA: group only",
    "Geo: lat/long",

]
vals = [
    secondary["ca_rf"]["roc_auc"],

]

horizontal_bars(
    ax,
    labels,
    vals,
    xlabel="Cross-validated ROC-AUC",

    vlines={"Chance = .500": 0.5},
    xlim=(0.45, 0.68),
)
fig.tight_layout()
plt.show()
```

*Note.* Stratified 5-fold CV, `random_state=42`, N = 241. Detailed results: [`memos/geo_predicts_transit.md`](memos/geo_predicts_transit.md); [`memos/ca_scores_predict_transit.md`](memos/ca_scores_predict_transit.md).

### Q27 and Q28 as traditional ML predictors of regular transit

@fig-q27-q28-prev and @tbl-q27-q28-auc summarize the Q27/Q28 reverse-prediction results ([memo](memos/q27_q28_predict_transit.md)). **Q28** (ride-share days) shows a monotonic prevalence gradient from **15.7%** regular (Never) to **94.1%** regular (8+ days/month) and CV ROC-AUC = **0.762** (AP = 0.689; balanced accuracy = 0.730; F1 = 0.702). **Q27** (rides on a typical transit day) yields CV ROC-AUC = **0.589**. The joint Q27+Q28 forest reaches AUC = **0.761** (Δ = −0.001 vs Q28 alone).

```{python}

q27["level"] = pd.Categorical(q27["level"], categories=order27, ordered=True)
q27 = q27.sort_values("level")
q28 = pd.DataFrame(secondary["q28_prevalence"])
q28["level"] = pd.Categorical(q28["level"], categories=order28, ordered=True)
q28 = q28.sort_values("level")

fig, axes = plt.subplots(1, 2, figsize=(9.6, 4.0))
for ax, frame, title in [
    (axes[0], q27, "Q27 (n = 239)"),

]:

## Extended secondary results: wave-2 follow-up experiments

Wave-1 memos left concrete open questions (unused Prolific demographics; country vs coordinates; Q28 after car conditioning; psych vs mobility importance; country×car; Q27 within regular riders; fair common-*N* rankings; residual CA after Q28). Eight offline experiments address those gaps with the same matched cohort and RF / Welch toolkit (`ca-personas followup-experiments --seed 42`). The agenda and methods hub are [`docs/research_memo_agenda.md`](docs/research_memo_agenda.md) and [`docs/secondary_rq_followup_experiments.md`](docs/secondary_rq_followup_experiments.md).

![Wave-2 follow-up experiment overview](memos/figures/followup_experiments_overview.png){fig-alt="Horizontal bar chart of primary CV ROC-AUC for eight extended follow-up experiments with chance, geo, CA, and Q28 reference lines."}

### Overview of seeded results

| Experiment | Memo | n | ROC-AUC | Takeaway |
|---|---|---:|---:|---|
| CA + Q28 + car (joint) | [memo](memos/ca_mobility_joint_predicts_transit.md) | 149 | **0.736** | Mobility-dominated joint model |
| Q28 \| car (nested) | [memo](memos/q28_conditioned_on_car.md) | 149 | **0.730** | Q28 retains lift; car adds +0.066 AUC |
| Country + car | [memo](memos/country_car_predicts_transit.md) | 149 | **0.699** | Place × auto access synergy |
| Common-*N* best (Q28) | [memo](memos/common_n_head_to_head.md) | 139 | **0.659** | Rideshare ranking robust to equal *N* |
| Demographics (Age+Sex+Student) | [memo](memos/demographics_predict_transit.md) | 224 | **0.618** | Age-driven modest signal (younger 57.1% vs older 24.6% regular) |
| Residual CA (CA-only arm) | [memo](memos/residual_ca_after_rideshare.md) | 241 | **0.590** | CA-only AUC; joint CA+Q28 = 0.783 (+0.021 over Q28) |
| Country only | [memo](memos/country_predicts_transit.md) | 241 | **0.552** | Ties lat/long geo |
| Q27 intensity among riders | [memo](memos/q27_intensity_among_riders.md) | 95–101 | **0.549** | No useful within-rider classifier |

### Findings that change interpretation of the `transit` tier

1. **Q28 is not just “no car.”** On the car-complete overlap (n=149), Q28 alone AUC = 0.665 and Q28+Q21 = 0.730—ride-share days retain discrimination after car conditioning, and car access adds +0.066 AUC ([nested memo](memos/q28_conditioned_on_car.md)).

2. **Fair rankings still crown rideshare.** Forcing Q28, car, country, geo, employment, CA, and demographics onto one complete-case frame (n=139) preserves **Q28 > country > car > geo > employment ≈ CA ≈ demos** ([common-*N* memo](memos/common_n_head_to_head.md)).

3. **Demographics matter for bias audits.** Age+Sex+Student reach AUC = 0.618 on n=224; younger tertiles are far more often weekly+ riders (57.1% vs 24.6% older). That is relevant to whether `demos`-tier LLM errors track age stereotyping ([demographics memo](memos/demographics_predict_transit.md)). Note this Age+Sex+Student feature set differs from the comprehensive-memo “demographics” ablation that also includes country (AUC = 0.636).

4. **CA is descriptively real, predictively redundant with Q28.** The overall regular-rider CA gap replicates (group Δ = −2.72, *d* = −0.46), but nesting CA with Q28 lifts AUC only from 0.762 → 0.783. Within Q28 strata the CA gap is heterogeneous—including a sign reversal in the 0–1 days cell ([residual CA memo](memos/residual_ca_after_rideshare.md)).

5. **Q27 remains weak even as an among-rider outcome.** High intensity among weekly+ riders is not recoverable from CA, Q28, car, employment, or demos (best AUC = 0.549).

6. **Kitchen-sink ceiling still looks like Q28.** A tuned comprehensive forest over demos + employment + geo + car + ride-share + CA reaches CV ROC-AUC = **0.824**, but permutation importance remains Q28-dominated ([comprehensive memo](memos/comprehensive_predictors_transit.md)).

# Discussion

On the full matched analytic cohort (**N = 241**), the framework makes the research contrasts concrete: each participant yields five persona prompts (`demos` → `employment` → `geo` → `transit` → `full`) with fixed ground-truth PRCA scores. The base `demos` layer includes **student status** alongside age, sex, and country of residence. Under the deterministic mock provider, group-CA MAE moves from **`{python} f"{MAE_GROUP_DEMOS:.2f}"`** (`demos`) to **`{python} f"{MAE_GROUP_TRANSIT:.2f}"`** (`transit`), while remaining well above the classical ML suite floor of **4.49** group MAE / **4.25** interpersonal MAE at the same tier ([`docs/ml_baselines.md`](docs/ml_baselines.md); [`memos/feature_predictive_power_ml_llm.md`](memos/feature_predictive_power_ml_llm.md)). Residual MAE differences by student status (base demos) and employment status (RQ1) are the stereotyping diagnostics once a live LLM provider replaces the mock.

Secondary analyses quantify what the `transit` tier contributes. Regular riders have lower group CA (Δ = −2.72, d = −0.46, p = .0003) and interpersonal CA (Δ = −1.73, d = −0.30, p = .020) ([`memos/transit_riders_ca.md`](memos/transit_riders_ca.md)). As reverse classifiers of weekly+ transit, survey coordinates (AUC = 0.551) and CA scores (AUC = 0.590) remain near chance, whereas **Q28 ride-share days** reach AUC = **0.762** and dominate Q27 (AUC = 0.589) in joint models ([`memos/q27_q28_predict_transit.md`](memos/q27_q28_predict_transit.md)). Wave-2 follow-ups strengthen that claim: Q28 retains lift after car access, still ranks first on a common-*N* frame, and leaves CA with only marginal incremental AUC ([`docs/secondary_rq_followup_experiments.md`](docs/secondary_rq_followup_experiments.md)). That asymmetry supports treating ride-share exposure—not transit-day intensity alone—as the high-value mobility cue in both tabular baselines and persona prompts ([`docs/factor_feature_importance.md`](docs/factor_feature_importance.md) likewise ranks Q28 first for predicting CA). Age-linked demographic structure in reverse transit prediction also flags the `demos` tier as a natural surface for stereotyping audits.

Limitations include (a) mock rather than production LLM predictions for the Posit MAE figures, (b) same-wave observational designs for reverse-prediction AUCs, which cannot establish that ride-share causes weekly+ transit (or vice versa), and (c) complete-case shrinkage for car-conditioned follow-ups. Those constraints keep Cloud builds keyless; they do not change the measurement design or the seeded full-cohort ML findings cited above.

```bash
python -m venv .venv
source .venv/bin/activate
pip install -r requirements.txt
pip install -e .
# Stage File A/B/C under ../sibling_data or CA_SIBLING_DATA=/tmp/sibling_data
ca-personas run --provider mock --join inner
ca-personas covariate-transit-rf --join inner --seed 42
python scripts/sync_posit_full_cohort_artifacts.py
quarto render
```
